title: Device-Aware Test: A Means to Attack Unmodelled Defects (Invited)
problem: Structural testing at advanced technology nodes and for emerging device technologies is insufficient to screen unmodeled defects, resulting in reduced outgoing product quality.
motivation: Recent manufacturing data reveals that traditional structural testing inadequately captures defects in advanced nodes and novel device technologies, requiring novel test approaches.
method: Device-Aware Test (DAT) adds a second layer to traditional manufacturing testing, which only checks if circuits are wired correctly. DAT uses models of actual transistor physics—how semiconductors behave, especially at tiny technology sizes—to design tests that expose defects these physical models predict. By grounding tests in real device behavior rather than just logical structure, DAT catches defects that traditional structural testing misses.
key_novelty: Device-Aware Test shifts from testing based purely on circuit logic to testing based on actual transistor device physics.
contributions: Application to multiple emerging device flavors
Potential extension beyond manufacturing test to broader validation contexts
primary_theme: Device-aware manufacturing test for unmodeled defects
